title: Scheme types and the SEBI categories
objectives: Differentiate open-ended, closed-ended and interval schemes.
Name the five SEBI scheme groups.
body_md:
## By structure

| Type | Features |
|---|---|
| **Open-ended** | Buy and sell any time at NAV; no fixed maturity |
| **Closed-ended** | Fixed tenure; units are listed on an exchange (or repurchase offered); bought only in the NFO |
| **Interval** | Combines both; opens for trading at specified intervals |

## SEBI categories (October 2017)

SEBI grouped schemes into five groups and made each AMC offer **one scheme per category** (with limited exceptions).

1. **Equity** schemes
2. **Debt** schemes
3. **Hybrid** schemes
4. **Solution-oriented** schemes (retirement, children's)
5. **Other** schemes (index funds, ETFs, fund of funds)

## Plans and options

- **Direct** and **Regular** plans; the direct plan has a lower expense ratio.
- **Growth** and **IDCW** (income distribution cum capital withdrawal) options; IDCW is paid from the scheme's own money and is not a guaranteed return.

> **Exam tip:** Dividend is now called IDCW; payouts reduce NAV.
example: A closed-ended fund can be bought only in its NFO. After that, the investor sells on the exchange at the market price, which may be below NAV.
say: Direct plans have lower costs because they carry no distributor commission.
IDCW is paid out of your own investment; it is not extra return.
never: Closed-ended funds can be redeemed at NAV any day.

check.q: Units of a closed-ended scheme are usually:
check.why: Closed-ended units are listed (or repurchase offers are made).

check.q: Which is NOT one of the five SEBI scheme groups?
check.why: The five groups are equity, debt, hybrid, solution-oriented and other.
IDCW replaced the term 'dividend' for MF payouts.
